svg.title: A private time saving can impose greater shared delay
svg.desc: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. A commuter switching to the shortcut saves personal time while existing shortcut users together incur more added delay. A load-dependent charge can attach that external cost to the decision. Roads, travelers, and the departure window stay fixed in the illustration. Change: Attach imposed delay to the route choice, or allocate access through a feasible alternative. Limitation: Measurement, collection, differing means, access, and diversion matter. No road capacity is added.

text.tspan: A private time saving can impose greater shared delay
Hypothetical example · qualitative relationships
One commuter switches from detour to shortcut
Switching commuter
Saves personal journey time.
Existing shortcut users
Combined added delay exceeds that
saving.
The driver counts the private saving but does not automatically bear the delay imposed on others.
These are stipulated comparisons, not measured travel times.
Change the switching decision · same roads and travelers
Load-dependent charge
Reflect the extra delay imposed on others.
Compare time and charge
The earlier saving may no longer favor
switching.
Upper cards compare consequences of one switch, not successive trips. Lower arrows show the proposed
change to decision costs. No card size represents elapsed time.
Change: Attach imposed delay to the route choice, or allocate access through a feasible
alternative.
Limit: Measurement, collection, differing means, access, and diversion matter. No road capacity is
added.
